prompt: A response carries `Cache-Control: no-cache`. What may the browser do with it?

choices.text: Keep it, and ask the server before each use
choices.why: Right. It may keep a copy, and the question it asks is answered by a `304` or a `200`.

choices.text: Keep it for a default time the browser chooses
choices.why: A time comes from `max-age`; `no-cache` gives the copy no time at all without a check.

choices.text: Use it for the rest of the session without asking
choices.why: Using a copy without asking is what `max-age` allows, for as many seconds as it names.

choices.text: Keep nothing and fetch it again every time
choices.why: That is `no-store`. The name `no-cache` misleads exactly this way.

prompt: A browser sends `If-None-Match` with the `ETag` it holds, and the file has not changed. What comes back?

choices.text: `200` with the whole file again
choices.why: That is the answer when the fingerprint no longer matches.

choices.text: Nothing; the browser does not send the request
choices.why: Under `no-cache` the request is sent; it is the body of the answer that is saved.

choices.text: `304 Not Modified`, with no body
choices.why: Right. The capture showed it for `style.css`: headers and nothing else.

choices.text: `404`, because the copy is in the browser already
choices.why: A `404` says the address does not exist; the file does.

prompt: Match each header to what it tells the browser.

pairs.right: Use the copy without asking for ten minutes
Keep a copy, and ask before using it
A fingerprint to quote when asking

prompt: A site serves `app.3f9c1a.js` with `max-age` set to a year. A new release changes the script. Why do returning visitors still get the new one?

choices.text: A release clears every visitor's cache
choices.why: A server has no way to reach into a browser's cache.

choices.text: They do not; they wait a year
choices.why: They would, if the name stayed the same. Here it does not.

choices.text: The browser checks the `ETag` once a day
choices.why: Within `max-age` the browser checks nothing; that is the point of it.

choices.text: The new release has a new file name, so a new address
choices.why: Right. The cache is keyed by address, and the page now asks for one never seen.

prompt: After the offer changed, the second visit in `stale.mjs` still showed Mango. What did the shop's log show for it?

choices.text: A `GET /api/offer` answered with the old offer
choices.why: The server had the new offer by then; had it been asked, it would have said Banana.

choices.text: No `GET /api/offer` at all
choices.why: Right. The browser answered from its copy, so the request never reached the shop.

choices.text: A `304` for `/api/offer`
choices.why: The offer has no `ETag`, and inside `max-age` the browser does not ask anyway.

choices.text: An error, because the page failed to load
choices.why: The page loaded and drew an offer: the old one.

prompt: The browser reported `200 /api/offer` on every visit. What does that status tell you?

choices.text: That the request was revalidated
choices.why: A revalidation shows as `304` in the shop's log, and there was none for the offer.

choices.text: That the server answered each time
choices.why: The server log has the request once; the other answers came from the cache.

choices.text: Nothing about whether the server was asked
choices.why: Right. A copy is reported with the status it was stored with, so the server's log is the evidence.

choices.text: That the offer is fresh
choices.why: The page said Mango after the change; a `200` and a stale answer go together fine.

prompt: The offer was first fetched at 10:00, and changed on the server at 10:04. For how many more minutes after 10:04 may a browser that kept it show the old one?
hint: `max-age=600` counts from when the copy was received.

prompt: Why does the first test in `tests/cache.spec.js` pass although the offer is cached for ten minutes?

choices.text: Its page lives in a new context with an empty cache
choices.why: Right. Every test is a first visit, so there is no copy to be stale.

choices.text: Playwright switches off caching in headless mode
choices.why: The returning-customer test runs headless too, and it met the cache.

choices.text: `toContainText` retries until the cache expires
choices.why: It retries for five seconds; the copy lasts six hundred.

choices.text: The `request` fixture clears the browser's cache
choices.why: `request` sends HTTP requests outside the browser; it touches no cache.

prompt: Which visitor in `visitors.mjs` was still shown Mango after the change?

choices.text: None of them; a second `goto` always refetches
choices.why: The same page visited again was shown Mango too.

choices.text: A new context made from the first one's saved storage state
choices.why: Storage state carries cookies and local storage, not the HTTP cache.

choices.text: A plain new context
choices.why: An empty cache asks the server, which had the new offer.

choices.text: A new page in the same context
choices.why: Right. Pages in one context share one cache.

prompt: A team saves a logged-in `storageState` and reuses it in every test so that nobody logs in twice. Does that make their tests returning customers as far as the cache goes?

choices.text: Yes, but only for files with an `ETag`
choices.why: No part of the HTTP cache travels in the state, with a fingerprint or without one.

choices.text: No; each test still starts with an empty cache
choices.why: Right. Logged in and first visit at once, which no real customer is.

choices.text: No, because `storageState` disables caching
choices.why: It disables nothing; the new context simply starts without a cache.

choices.text: Yes; the state includes everything the browser kept
choices.why: It includes cookies and local storage. The saved-state visitor was shown the new offer.

prompt: Put the steps of the returning-customer test in order.
items: Open the offer page and see the mango
Set a new offer through the API
Open the page again in the same context
trap: Setting the offer before the first visit makes it a first-time visitor's test again: nothing old was kept.

prompt: What does `test.fail()` do to the returning-customer test?

choices.text: It expects a failure, and reports one if the test passes
choices.why: Right. Green while the flaw exists, red the day somebody fixes it, which is the reminder to remove the mark.

choices.text: It retries the test until it passes
choices.why: Retries are `--retries`; they would never get past a stale copy kept for ten minutes.

choices.text: It turns the failure into a warning that the run ignores
choices.why: The run does not ignore it: it counts as passed only while it fails as expected.

choices.text: It skips the test until the flaw is fixed
choices.why: That is `test.skip()`. This test runs every time.

prompt: Why check the `Cache-Control` header with the `request` fixture rather than with a page?

choices.text: Because headers differ between Chromium and other browsers
choices.why: The server sends the same headers whichever browser asks.

choices.text: Because `request` follows the cache rules of the browser
choices.why: It follows none, which is exactly why it is useful here.

choices.text: Because a page cannot read response headers
choices.why: It can, through `response.headers()`; the difference is the cache in between.

choices.text: Because `request` keeps no cache, so it always asks the server
choices.why: Right. It sees exactly the promise the server makes, in milliseconds, with no browser.

A test intercepts `/api/products` with `page.route` to watch the request. What else changes for that page?

choices.text: The page uses a new context
choices.why: The page stays in its context; what goes is its cache.

choices.text: Nothing; a route that only continues is invisible
choices.why: The last test in `tests/cache.spec.js` changes nothing in its route and still passes where the plain one fails.

choices.text: The HTTP cache is switched off
choices.why: Right. Playwright's reference says so in a note on `route`, and the routing test shows it.

prompt: A test needs the cache off in Firefox as well as Chromium. Which of these does that?

choices.text: `Network.setCacheDisabled` through a DevTools Protocol session
choices.why: Only Chromium speaks that protocol.

choices.text: A new context for the test
choices.why: Right. It is the default, and it works the same in every browser Playwright drives.

choices.text: The Disable cache box in DevTools
choices.why: It works while the panel is open, by hand, and a test opens no panel.

choices.text: Playwright's `--disable-cache` flag
choices.why: Playwright 1.56 has no such flag.

prompt: Tests pass on a laptop and fail on staging, which sits behind a CDN. The failing check is that a just-changed price appears. What is worth asking first?

choices.text: Whether staging runs a slower browser
choices.why: Slowness delays an answer; it does not bring back an old price.

choices.text: Whether the laptop has Disable cache ticked
choices.why: That box acts only while DevTools is open, and tests open none.

choices.text: Whether Playwright reused a context between tests
choices.why: Each test gets a new context in both places; the browser is the same.

choices.text: Whether the CDN kept the old response
choices.why: Right. A new context empties the browser's cache, not one outside the browser.

prompt: Which of these visitors met the stale offer in this lesson's runs? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The same page, reloaded
choices.why: Right. A reload revalidated the page and reused the offer's copy.

choices.text: A new context with saved storage state
choices.why: Saved state carries no cache, so it asked the server.

choices.text: A kept profile, reopened
choices.why: Right. A persistent context keeps its cache on disk between launches.

choices.text: A test whose page used `page.route`
choices.why: Routing switched its cache off, so it saw the banana.

prompt: Somebody fixes `/api/offer` to send `no-cache`. What happens on the next run of `tests/cache.spec.js`, unchanged?

choices.text: The two marked tests are reported as failures
choices.why: Right. They now pass, which is not what they were marked to do, and that tells you to remove `test.fail`.

choices.text: The routing test starts to fail
choices.why: It saw the new offer before the fix and sees it after.

choices.text: The static file test fails, since `no-cache` is now on the offer too
choices.why: It reads `style.css`, which the fix does not touch.

choices.text: Everything passes, and the marks can stay
choices.why: Two tests are marked to fail; once they pass, Playwright reports them.

prompt: A tester wants to know whether a defect report about an old price is a cache problem. What is the cheapest first step?

choices.text: Add `page.route` to the existing test
choices.why: That switches the cache off and hides the very thing in question.

choices.text: Run the suite with `--retries 3`
choices.why: Each retry is a new context again; none of them is a returning customer.

choices.text: Read the response's `Cache-Control` header
choices.why: Right. One `curl -i` shows the promise the server made, and `max-age` on a price is the answer.

choices.text: Write a test with a new context
choices.why: A new context is a first visit, the one case where the cache cannot show.
